title: Refinement of the zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity assay
author: Hoyberghs, Bars, et al.
materials: Preincubate the test compound (one or more concentrations) with human liver microsomes (pooled, 50 donors, Thermo Fischer scientific, USA) at 200 µg/ml and NADPH tetrasodium salt (1.25 mM) in embryo medium for 1 h at 28.5 °C. In addition to the test suspension(s), include a medium control and a blank control, i.e. the preincubation mix without test compound.14′. After 1 h preincubation, the test suspension and blank control are ultracentrifuged at 100 000 x g for 1 h at 4 °C.14″. Pipet the supernatant of the blank control and the test suspension, containing the test compound and its metabolites, and dilute the supernatant 1:10 in embryo medium.15–

To test this part of our protocol, we used carbamazepine as tool compound. Carbamazepine is an anti-epileptic drug and a human teratogen. It is believed that its metabolite carbamazepine-10–11-epoxide is causing the malformations. As depicted in Table 7, we used 4 conditions, i.e. 250 µM carbamazepine (Sigma-Aldrich, Diegem, Belgium) and 125 µM carbamazepine-10–11-epoxide (Sigma-Aldrich, Diegem, Belgium) as internal controls for our analytical measurement, undiluted supernatant after step 14′ to assess consumption of carbamazepine and our test solution, 1:10 diluted supernatant after ultracentrifugation of the preincubation mix, to determine the actual concentration of the metabolite carbamazepine-10–11-epoxide in our mZEDTA. Prior to the analysis of the test conditions, we determined the stability of 500 µM carbamazepine in embryo medium (according to the stability protocol in our ZEDTA). Uptake by the zebrafish embryos was not assessed, as a dose-response in morphological defects had already been established by others for this compound [12].Table 7Identification of the samples that were analyzed with LC-MS for presence of carbamazepine and carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide.Table 7Sample ContentEstimated molar concentration (µM)Estimated mass concentration (µg/ml)Parent (Carbamazepine)250 µM59.0 µg/mlUltracentrifuged (UC'ed) preincubation mixture (Carbamazepine)250 µM59.0 µg/ml1/10 Ultracentrifuged (UC'ed) preincubation mixture (Carbamazepine)25 µM5.90 µg/mlHuman metabolite (Carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide)125 µM31.5 µg/ml
The following analytical protocol was used:

First, the carbamazepine samples (parent and ultracentrifuged preincubation mixture in Table 7) were diluted in water (HPLC grade) by a factor of 10. These diluted samples were once again diluted by a factor of 10 in 70:30 (v/v) water:acetonitrile (HPLC grade) containing 0.39 µM lamotrigine (Sigma-Aldrich, Diegem, Belgium) as an internal standard. In order to quantify the concentrations of carbamazepine and carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide in these samples, standard curves (in replicate) for carbamazepine (17.5 - 50,000 ng/mL) and carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide (1.7 – 50,000 ng/mL) were prepared. These samples were subsequently diluted by a factor of 10 in water:acetonitrile containing 0.39 µM lamotrigine. The samples were then stored at −80 °C upon use.

steps.title: Stability assessment incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare test concentrations in embryo medium (see step 14 of ZEDTA) and incubate at 28.5 °C ± 0.2 °C.

steps.title: Collect stability samples
steps.instruction: Take samples for analysis at 0 h, 24 h and 120 h and send to the bioanalytical laboratory; volume and dilution steps follow the laboratory’s method.

steps.title: Check 24 h degradation
steps.instruction: If the test solution is degraded by more than 20 % of the nominal concentration at 24 h, consider the compound too unstable and do not proceed further.

steps.title: Apply semi‑static exposure if needed
steps.instruction: If degradation exceeds 20 % at 120 h, adopt a semi‑static exposure: renew test solutions every 24 h (step 15 of ZEDTA).

steps.title: Uptake sampling of embryos
steps.instruction: Sample zebrafish embryos (see steps 1–11 of ZEDTA for collection) that have been exposed from 5.25 hpf onward, at 24 hpf and at 120 hpf; number of embryos follows the bioanalytical method.

steps.title: Perform bioanalytical washing steps
steps.instruction: Apply the washing protocol and any further preparatory steps supplied by the bioanalytical laboratory.

steps.title: Bioanalytical analysis of internal levels
steps.instruction: The bioanalytical laboratory analyses and reports the internal concentrations of the test compound in the embryos.

steps.title: Abort if no uptake detected
steps.instruction: If analytical data show no uptake at both 24 hpf and 120 hpf, stop the experiment.

steps.title: Interpret internal concentration changes
steps.instruction: If internal concentrations at 120 hpf are lower or higher than at 24 hpf and this cannot be explained by stability data, note metabolism or accumulation for interpretation in step 16 of ZEDTA.

steps.title: Proceed to main ZEDTA protocol
steps.instruction: Continue with the standard ZEDTA protocol described below.

steps.title: Maintain breeding stock
steps.instruction: Keep adult zebrafish (Danio rerio, AB line, GIGA, University of Liège) in tanks of approximately 50 L.

steps.title: Set water parameters
steps.instruction: Adjust water to 28.5 °C ± 0.2 °C; conductivity 500 ± 25 µS/cm using Instant Ocean sea salts; pH 7.5 ± 0.3 with NaHCO₃.

steps.title: Renew water on waste detection
steps.instruction: Renew water when ammonia, nitrite or nitrate become detectable.

steps.title: Apply light/dark cycle
steps.instruction: Implement a 14 h light / 10 h dark photoperiod.

steps.title: Feed fish twice daily
steps.instruction: Feed thawed food (Artemia nauplii, Daphnia, Chironomidae larvae or Chaoborus larvae) twice daily and granulated food at 2 % of mean wet weight per feeding, also twice daily.

steps.title: Net fish before mating
steps.instruction: Place fish in a net in the tank the day before mating to prevent egg predation.

steps.title: Allow spawning period
steps.instruction: The following morning, allow fish to spawn and fertilize eggs for about 45 min.

steps.title: Collect fertilized eggs
steps.instruction: Siphon fertilized eggs from the tank bottom with a tube.

steps.title: Rinse embryos in embryo medium
steps.instruction: Remove feces and coagulated eggs; rinse remaining embryos in embryo medium (0.294 g CaCl₂·H₂O, 0.123 g MgSO₄·7H₂O, 0.059 g NaHCO₃, 0.005 g KCl, 0.1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.5 dissolved in 1 L RO water).

steps.title: Check early cell division
steps.instruction: Examine embryos under a stereomicroscope for normal cell division within 2 hpf.

steps.title: Discard abnormal embryos
steps.instruction: Discard unfertilized or asymmetric embryos and replace them with healthy ones until enough embryos are obtained (see step 14).

steps.title: Plate embryos in 48‑well plates
steps.instruction: Randomly transfer selected embryos (one per well) into a 48‑well plate containing at least 500 µL embryo medium per well.

steps.title: Validate fertilization and mortality rates
steps.instruction: The experiment is valid when fertilization rate > 90 % and control mortality < 10 % at the end of the experiment.

steps.title: Allocate embryos per replicate and concentrations
steps.instruction: Use 20 embryos per replicate (2 replicates performed in different weeks) for each control (medium and/or solvent) and each test group; typically test three concentrations (Low, Mid, High) but numbers may be reduced or increased as needed (≥5 concentrations for full concentration‑response curves).

steps.title: Rear controls and expose test groups
steps.instruction: Rear medium‑control embryos in embryo medium until 120 hpf. At 5.25 hpf transfer solvent controls and test groups from embryo medium into the respective solvent (usually 0.1 % DMSO) or test solution and keep them there until 120 hpf. If using a solvent other than 0.1 % DMSO, first perform a solvent‑control experiment.

steps.title: Morphological evaluation at defined timepoints
steps.instruction: Assess embryos at 5.25, 10, 24, 48, 72, 96 and 120 hpf for the morphological parameters listed in Table 2. Use the 5.25 hpf timepoint to monitor embryo quality. Anesthetize larvae at 96 and 120 hpf with MS‑222 (0.2 g/L in embryo medium) for scoring. Score 0 for normal morphology and 1 for abnormal morphology using the binary classification in Supplementary Figs. 1–8.

steps.title: Euthanize larvae after scoring
steps.instruction: After the final gross‑morphology scoring, euthanize larvae with an overdose of MS‑222 (1 g/L in embryo medium) or, alternatively, by hypothermic shock in ice water for at least 12 h.

steps.title: Metabolic preincubation with microsomes
steps.instruction: Preincubate each test concentration with pooled human liver microsomes (50 donors, Thermo Fisher) at 200 µg/mL and NADPH tetrasodium salt (1.25 mM) in embryo medium for 1 h at 28.5 °C. Include a medium control and a blank control (microsomes + NADPH without test compound).

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge incubation mixtures
steps.instruction: After the 1 h preincubation, ultracentrifuge the test suspension and the blank control at 100 000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dilute supernatants for exposure
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant from the blank control and the test suspension, then dilute each 1:10 in embryo medium before use in exposure.

steps.title: Continue with standard ZEDTA steps
steps.instruction: Proceed with the remaining steps of the ZEDTA protocol (embryo handling, exposure, evaluation, etc.).

steps.title: Increase compound concentration if negative
steps.instruction: If no adverse effects are observed, increase the test‑compound concentration (up to substrate inhibition) in the preincubation step and repeat steps 28–31.

steps.title: Concentrate test solution for low metabolites
steps.instruction: If metabolite concentrations remain low (typically < µM), concentrate the test solution (e.g., evaporate a volatile solvent such as methanol) before re‑testing.

steps.title: Transfer larvae for skeletal staining
steps.instruction: At 120 hpf, move larvae into a small petri dish and discard the surrounding solution.

steps.title: Stain larvae with Alizarin Red
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of 0.005 % Alizarin Red solution to the petri dish and incubate for 1 h.

steps.title: Wash stained larvae
steps.instruction: Remove the Alizarin Red solution and wash the larvae in embryo medium.

steps.title: Anesthetize larvae before embedding
steps.instruction: Transfer larvae to MS‑222 (0.2 g/L in embryo medium) until they lose dorsal‑ventral balance.

steps.title: Embed and image larvae
steps.instruction: Embed larvae in 1 % low‑gelling temperature agar containing 0.2 g/L MS‑222. Image with an Olympus SZX16 (6.3×) using RFP at 620 nm, 100 ms exposure, µManager v1.4, 8 images per stack, two positions (lateral and dorsoventral), 3 s intervals, captured with a Zyla 4.2 sCMOS camera.

steps.title: Euthanize larvae post‑imaging
steps.instruction: Euthanize the imaged larvae with an overdose of MS‑222 (1 g/L in embryo medium) or by hypothermic shock for at least 12 h.

steps.title: Score bone intensity and shape
steps.instruction: Process images in ImageJ. Score bone intensity (0 = no stain, 1 = weak, 2 = moderate, 3 = heavy) and shape (0 = normal, 1 = malformed) for each structure listed in Table 3. For each bone, select the image with the highest intensity score to determine the final score.
